title: EvalDocResult
description: Output of `model eval` — the runtime verdict over a document INSTANCE: which rules fired on the data, via the native-safe interpreter (the sole runtime eval engine on every target). By default this is full validation. `--relevant <json>` selects partial validation: a JSON array of current-page field/group instance paths; `[0]` or `[*]` means every repetition (ALL_SEMANTIC), while `[n]` selects one 1-based row. An OMITTED index on a repeatable segment is refused — it means repetition 1 in A12 and used to mean ALL here, so state which you mean. Global fields are auto-relevant. The INPUT --instance shape is NOT restated here — it is `document-instance.schema.json`, served as the `input` half of `dmtool schema model eval`.

validationMode.description: present only when `--relevant` selected partial validation; absent means full validation. Structural over-repetition findings do not by themselves make ancestor groups erroneous for partial counts; in-capacity invalid values still can. Nonempty partial selections report structural over-repetition outside the selection, including present null/empty fields; an empty selection emits no structural findings. Starred value-list extent and NumberOfValueInFields accept wildcard or complete declared-slot coverage; selecting every held row is insufficient when the declaration allows more. A clean, empty parent group becomes provably empty when selected descendants jointly cover every declared finite repetition combination and every descendant field; held rows do not set that denominator. Starred group absence requires coverage of missing declared positions; an included positive row remains decisive. Keyed lower stars bind the matched parent, while a missing parent requires wildcard coverage there. Parallel rules compress differing error-selector coordinates to wildcards for dispatch, retaining original operand relevance. With ordinary outer/frame iteration, a concrete joined error coordinate suppresses dispatch; conflicting joined selectors can restore it. Without ordinary iteration, an error selector admits all keys.

fired.description: the distinct error codes that fired, in first-seen order

messages.description: every message occurrence the evaluation raised, in evaluation order; occurrences are not deduplicated even when numeric parallel iteration renders two tokens for the same matched rows. Evaluated by the dm interpreter — the envelope's `engine` names who produced these

rule.description: present only when narrowed to one rule (--rule or a candidate --condition/--field)

fired.description: whether that rule fired on the document

unsupported.description: present only when the engine could NOT evaluate some construct — a CustomCondition with no registered impl, or a custom-typed value with no --predefined-types entry. Reported here, NOT silently absent from `fired` (which would read as a clean pass) — G29. `--strict-custom` turns a non-empty `unsupported` into a refusal (exit 2).

name.description: what could not be evaluated — read it according to `subject`, since the two kinds are different addresses

subject.description: element = a model path (a rule/computation/field declaration, no repetition); cell = a canonical A12 instance pointer to a document cell. Published because the two used to share one key with nothing to tell them apart, so neither a consumer nor the renderer could treat the pointer half as a pointer

code.description: the rule's error code, or a kernel formal-error code

rule.description: the firing rule's full slash-path (e.g. /Order/X); a kernel FORMAL check reports the sentinel 'formalePruefung' — a leading '/' is the author-rule discriminator

field.description: the offending field's address. A message address is A12's PartiallyKnownDocumentMultiPointer (what IMessage.getErrorFieldPointer returns), so it is published in canonical A12 pointer form — no leading slash, [1] omitted, e.g. Order/Items[2]/Count, paste-compatible with A12 addressing — exactly when it names one cell. It may instead carry a wildcard above the last part, or the -5 of a level that matched no row; A12 defines no pointer string for such a value, so it passes through as the interpreter house form (/Order[1]/Items[2]/Count) rather than being given an invented canonical spelling. Test the leading slash to tell the two apart

message.description: the INTERPOLATED end-user text — the authored message with $Field$/$Field.value$ tokens resolved against this document (what the user actually reads, G1)

referenced.description: the fields the rule READ (its operands) — A12's referencedFields. Same address contract as `field`: canonical A12 pointer when the address names one cell, house form otherwise

fillToFix.description: for an OMISSION error, the operand fields that can cause the omission, filled ones included (the kernel's refOmissionErrorResponsible); an operand read only by a presence check such as `FieldFilled` is referenced but never listed here. Absent for a VALUE error. Same address contract as `field`
